  "rationale": "The book’s core claim—that oil symbolizes proven works/obedience (the pressed fruit of the olive that fuels light) rather than the Holy Spirit—rests almost entirely on a forced reading of the ten-virgins parable plus Exodus 27:20, Proverbs 21:20 and Matthew 5:16. While the parable’s “buy” language does create a real tension with the Spirit-as-gift motif (Acts 8:20), that tension alone cannot overturn the broader biblical pattern in which oil is repeatedly and explicitly yoked to the Spirit’s anointing and empowerment (1 Sam 16:13; Isa 61:1/Luke 4:18; Acts 10:38; Zech 4:6; 2 Cor 1:21–22; 1 John 2:20, 27). The book never engages those primary texts; it simply asserts that the parable “refuses” the Spirit reading. The olive-tree-as-Israel and Gethsemane-as-oil-press links are evocative but midrashic, not exegetical demonstrations that oil itself = works. Consequently the central identification remains under-supported relative to the dominant scriptural usage, and the strongest counter-reading (Spirit/anointing) is left unanswered.",
